Causal dependency authority is process-local and cannot survive restart. packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:763-769 generates CAUSAL_DEPENDENCY_DECISION_KEY with randomBytes(32) at module load, while verifyCausalDependencyDecision at lines 924-948 recomputes the HMAC with that process-local key. Repro: create an advisory decision in one Node process, then import the same dist in a child and call verifyCausalDependencyDecision(decision, identity); the parent returns true and the child returns false. A signed/current CertificationWindow decision therefore becomes inadmissible after CLI or process restart, despite the acceptance contract requiring durable authority binding. Persist a stable authority key/signature or a verifiable durable authority artifact, and add a cross-process verification test.

Unknown input keys are silently excluded from dependency drift. packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:819-858 iterates each node.inputIds, but never checks keys present in currentInputHashes that are absent from the declared dependency DAG. Repro: evaluate a node declaring only declared=same while currentInputHashes also contains unmapped=changed, with materialHash changed and storyFilesHash unchanged; the function returns causalDecision=advisory, gateAdmissible=true, changedInputIds=[], and materialHashStrict=false. A changed dependency outside the declared nodes can therefore evade strict rerun or freshness handling. Enforce declared and current input-key completeness, or treat unknown keys as missing and take the strict materialHash fallback, with an adversarial test.

Receipt integrity is an unkeyed self-hash rather than authenticity. packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:359-365 and 368-384 accept any caller-recomputed SHA256 receiptHash; packages/main/src/core/store.ts:405-420 performs CAS checks under the supplied hash but adds no durable signature or authority binding. Repro: mutate persisted outputProbe from the original selector to EVIL, recompute receiptHash, update the index, and replay; the cache accepts EVIL with one child run, output {runs:1,first:pass,second:pass}. A local actor able to alter the artifact and index can manufacture a replayable PASS, violating tamper-resistant acceptance. Bind receipts to stable keyed authority or another non-caller-writable evidence source and add a tamper mutation test.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:272-280 [high] redactEnvironment uppercases every environment key before hashing the execution identity. On POSIX, effectiveValidationCommandEnvironment preserves case and the child process treats Path and PATH as distinct, but createCausalExecutionKey produces the same ce:v1 key and canonical PATH entry for both (repro on current HEAD: Path=a and PATH=a yield equal keys). A command whose behavior depends on a case-sensitive custom variable can therefore reuse a receipt under a different effective environment, violating the explicit environment identity and stale-cache acceptance=0 contract. Preserve POSIX key case and add a case-sensitive environment mutation test.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:608-619 [medium] The batch execution cache deletes an entry only when its promise resolves to a non-reusable receipt; if executeFresh rejects (for example a transient child/receipt-store I/O error), the derived batchReceipt remains a rejected promise in batch.executions. A later exact-key retry therefore returns the same rejection without invoking the child again (current-HEAD repro: first transient, second transient, runs=1). This permanently poisons the batch and violates the transaction/infra-failure retry contract; delete the same promise in a rejection handler and add a transient-error retry test.

packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:499-510,624-635 [high] createValidationCausalPreflightGate rechecks canonicalized preflight facts before each child, but probeVerifierIndex records only readable/path and never fingerprints the Git index bytes or identity. Replacing or changing .git/index between the initial PASS and child launch therefore leaves factsUnchanged true, so validate can launch an expensive child against a stale current-index contract, violating CHK-004:adversarial:0/1. Include an index content digest or equivalent index identity in the verifier facts and revalidation.

packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:1419-1431 [high] commitCanonicalCausalEvidence revalidate checks only head/material/storyFiles hashes and CAS index; it never re-reads the writer lease or validates the receipt command/effective-environment/selector-policy identity at canonical commit/retry. If the lease is revoked or expired or the execution identity changes after the preflight or child run, the checklist import still commits. This violates CHK-002 lease/index/material/identity revalidation; make the import transaction revalidate the complete writer and identity snapshot.

packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:1254-1363,2417-2476 [high] the re-executing stale-refresh path runs enforceAndStampEvidence outside the checklist lock, then writeStaleRefresh writes the pre-refresh head/material/storyFiles hashes and receipt directly with store.writeChecklist. It never recomputes current identity or passes the new receipt through commitCanonicalCausalEvidence/importCausalEvidenceReceipt. A material, lease, or index change while the command runs can therefore persist mechanical true evidence bound to a stale snapshot as if it were fresh. Revalidate and import the receipt atomically before the refresh write.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:608-620 [medium] the batch cache removes a non-reusable receipt only in the fulfillment branch. If executeFresh rejects, for example on a runner or spawn infrastructure error, batchReceipt rejects and remains in args.batch.executions, so every later same-key intent reuses the rejection and cannot retry or reach a later PASS. This is distinct from the resolved fail, timeout, or partial-output case covered by F-007; remove the entry on rejection or finally as well.

packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:640-642,905-931 [high] executeCausalEvidence verifies only the preflight report's self-signature and all-pass shape; CausalPreflightFacts carries no command, storyId, or execution-identity binding, and the core never compares the report to the key being executed. Repro: preflightCausalEvidence(all-pass facts) with no command field, followed by executeCausalEvidence with a different command identity and revalidateBeforeRun=()=>true, returned disposition=executed with runs=1. A preflight for another command/story, or a caller-synthesized all-pass report, can therefore pass the launch gate. Bind the signed preflight to the same execution identity/current probes or make the authoritative handler boundary unavoidable.

findings.desc: brand-path-decision-residue: packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts:139 (new B-5a15 entry runtime-causal-evidence-receipts) hardcodes deprecated brand literals inside a path DECISION regex: rx(String.raw "(?:^|/)(?:\.lattice|\.proof-or-stop)/story/actives/[^/]+/causal-evidence(?:/|$)|..."). WHY this is concept residue: every other state-dir-scoped entry in this same file derives its matcher from the resolver via stateDirExact()/stateDirPrefix() over STATE_DIR_NAMES (lines 110, 179, 188, 215, 224, 239, 348), which packages/main/src/core/brand-paths.ts:145 exports precisely so a state-dir rename needs no literal edits. This one entry freezes the two spellings inline, so the same concept is expressed two contradictory ways in one file. WHY it is currently un-gated: the lattice-residue [brand-decision] check PASSES (ran it: 0 hits) because makeBrandDecisionDetector in scripts/verify-lattice-residue.mjs:225-250 only recognizes .startsWith/.endsWith/.includes/.indexOf(<literal>) and ===/!== operand shapes; a RegExp-shaped path decision matches none of the three, so the check is vacuous for this line. Verified blast radius by probe: the matcher returns true today for .proof-or-stop/, .lattice/ and docs/story/ receipt paths, but false for any renamed state dir; on a future rename findRuntimeArtifactEntry misses, isMaterialExcludedRuntimeArtifactPath (line 423) returns false, and writing a CAS receipt would then move materialHash - exactly the failure the entry comment says it exists to prevent. Latent (rename-triggered), not a live defect today, hence medium and recorded rather than fixed in-story: the file is in allowedModify but no checklist item claims resolver-routing. Follow-up: route the matcher through STATE_DIR_NAMES, and teach the brand-decision detector the regex/path-decision shape so this whole class is gated instead of passing vacuously.

On a future state-dir rename findRuntimeArtifactEntry would miss, isMaterialExcludedRuntimeArtifactPath would return false, and writing a CAS receipt would move materialHash - the exact failure the entry exists to prevent. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: dedicated story that routes this entry through the resolver candidate list AND widens makeBrandDecisionDetector to recognise RegExp-shaped path decisions, since the gate blind spot is the more general defect. findings.resolvedReason: DEFERRED to a follow-up story after severity re-assessment; the finding is REAL but was graded on incomplete information. CONFIRMED: rerunEvidence has no production producer. causal-evidence.ts:1207 declares it and :1280 consumes it, but neither production caller supplies it - handlers/certification-window.ts:166-177 omits it entirely and core/evidence-freshness.ts:63 forwards an args type that does not include it. The producer helpers createCausalDependencyRerunEvidence (:1139) and causalDependencyExecutionInputs (:1122) have ZERO non-test callers repo-wide. So CHK-003's promised 'affected DAG nodes rerun at 100% with false-fresh=0' is unreachable outside hand-built unit fixtures. RE-ASSESSMENT (verified, and the reason this is deferred rather than fixed): no gate consumes affectedNodeRerun or falseFresh - the only non-test reader repo-wide is an assertion in causal-evidence-smoke.ts:138. They are REPORTED METRICS, not admission inputs. And the absence FAILS CLOSED: with no rerunEvidence, missingReruns is non-empty, so finalGateAdmissible at causal-evidence.ts:1292 computes false and every affected node is treated as stale. The missing producer makes the gate STRICTER, never laxer. BLAST RADIUS: no live defect, no false admission, no gate distortion. The exposure is a documentation/claim gap: CHK-003's context text promises a production metric the implementation does not deliver. WHY DEFERRED: not critical/high in effect, touches neither security nor data integrity, cannot distort a lifecycle gate, does not block acceptance. Building a real producer means minting per-node CAS receipts by actually re-executing each affected node and binding nodeId+inputHashes+storyId/materialHash/storyFilesHash into each signed receipt - substantial new machinery on shared causal infrastructure, claimed by no checklist item. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: a dedicated story that either (a) implements the per-node rerun-receipt producer end to end, or (b) narrows CHK-003's stated promise to what the fail-closed implementation actually delivers. Option (b) is the cheaper honest fix if the metric has no consumer. ESCALATE IF: any gate begins reading affectedNodeRerun or falseFresh for admission, at which point the absent producer would become a live correctness issue.

Verified against current code: certification-window.ts:110-129 deriveCertificationDomainInputHashes + :156-177 buildCertificationDecision now construct real per-domain nodes and non-empty currentInputHashes (fixed across 55a1e00343/0adc7c34ea/cfc8402e1f, landed after those findings were filed); causal-evidence.ts:1167-1179 verifyCausalDependencyRerunEvidence now requires storyId/materialHash/storyFilesHash to match currentIdentity (fixed in 8cae04f219 fix: bind causal rerun receipts to evaluation identity, timestamped after F-289/F-292 were filed). None of these ~20 findings are marked resolved. This creates real risk during REVIEW/TEST acceptance accounting: a human or automated pass over open findings cannot distinguish live defects from already-fixed ones without re-deriving the same trace this reviewer just did. Recommend the main agent re-verify each open finding against current HEAD and either finding_resolve (fixed, citing the landing commit) or explicitly re-confirm still-broken with a fresh repro before REVIEW->TEST.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/causal-evidence.test.mjs (verificationEvidence for CHK-004:happy:2 and CHK-004:happy:3, checklist.json): both should-priority intents carry evidence with result=pass and mechanical=false, with nonMechanicalReason explicitly stating the receipt was invalidated by verification_evidence_refresh_stale and the pinned command node --test packages/main/tests/causal-evidence.test.mjs was NOT re-run (evidence headHash=735f159f, stamped 2026-08-31T20:02:05Z, stale vs current HEAD 1f22cf4). Re-running that exact pinned command at current HEAD reproduces a live, reproducible failure of the F-247 and F-249-series tests: pre_review_check_read returns status=fail with codes including PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED, PR_PRODUCTION_PATH_UNPROVEN, PR_MUTATION_EVIDENCE_MISSING, PR_MUTATION_DID_NOT_BITE, PR_CONTROL_NOT_RESTORED, PR_TRANSCRIPT_MISSING, PR_AUTHORITY_INADMISSIBLE, none of which match either test's recognized bootstrap/fail-closed code allowlist, so the test throws AssertionError rather than passing. Commit 3c0b62c1d3 (fix: scope pre-review semantic bindings to the canonical cases they describe, which changed packages/main/src/core/pre-review-live-proof.ts isCanonicalPreReviewCaseId scoping consumed by this same check) claims in its message '34 positive assertions, 16 mutations all biting' but added zero test coverage, and the committed pre-review-check.json artifact (129d1206, 2026-09-01T04:13:09) predates that commit (13:43:12), so the artifact is stale relative to the code it is meant to certify. The should-priority evidence rows should not read result=pass while self-admitting non-mechanical/non-current status; this is the same underlying defect already tracked by open findings B-5a15:F-003/F-004/F-005/F-006 from the acceptance-chain angle, but is flagged here specifically as a verificationEvidence integrity gap: a should-intent's evidence record must not assert pass when it is simultaneously non-mechanical and reproducibly failing on live re-run of its own pinned command.

findings.resolvedReason: PARTIALLY MITIGATED. Reconciliation improved from 1 of 5 planned paths to 2 of 5 (CHK-001 and CHK-003, both relation=exact, confirmed by the RI-058 critic). pre_review_check_read moved from status=fail to status=inconclusive. Critically, it is NOT blocking: pre_review_check_read reports blocking=false and the DEV->REVIEW gate at transition-orchestrator.ts:131 throws only if report.blocking, so this finding never gated the transition - I had misread status=fail as a hard gate for several rounds before checking the field the gate actually consumes. WHAT WAS FIXED: three plannedPathDeclarations named consumers that provably do not consume the producer, and were corrected by the dispatched verification-intent role in PLAN. CHK-002 core/causal-evidence.ts#importCausalEvidenceReceipt (zero same-file callers) -> handlers/checklist.ts#commitCanonicalCausalEvidence (:1751,:1772). CHK-003 core/certification-window.ts#detectCertificationWindowMaterialDrift (that file has zero references to the producer) -> handlers/certification-window.ts#buildCertificationDecision (imports :19, calls :206). CHK-004 handlers/checklist.ts#enforceAndStampEvidence (non-exported, so endpointMatchesArtifactKind requires exported===1 and rejects it) -> handlers/verifier.ts#createValidationCausalPreflightGate (export at :617, imports :90, calls :670). CHK-003 additionally required widening the signed scope contract to admit handlers/certification-window.ts, justified as a PLAN-time omission: it carries 164 insertions across five of this story's own commits and was already an acknowledged out-of-scope change, but scopeAllows (acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:83-86) reads only the signed arrays and ignores acknowledgements. The RI-058 concept lane audited all 23 scope-contract revisions and confirmed allowedModify only ever grew (9 to 13 to 14) with mode=enforce throughout - no entry removed or relaxed. RESIDUAL, root-caused not guessed: producerConsumerRelation (acceptance-discovery-adapters.ts:1780-1786) matches an importedCall only when call.caller is a resolvable NAME. The three remaining consumers have none - a local const (checklist.ts:1606), an anonymous arrow callback (checklist.ts:2579), and a top-level script statement (causal-evidence-smoke.ts). I checked every in-scope alternative for each producer; none offers a named exported consumer. I deliberately did NOT declare core/evidence-freshness.ts#evaluateCausalEvidenceFreshness, which would have resolved a path instantly but has ZERO callers (dead code, finding F-332) - that would buy a green gate by making the contract less truthful, which the defect-triage rules forbid. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: a framework story on how plannedPathDeclarations should express producers consumed from anonymous callbacks, local consts, or top-level statements. Not fixable by editing this story's declarations without either restructuring production code purely to satisfy discovery, or declaring a dead path.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:527-608 (sameEvidenceSemantics vs sameAuditedAttestationIdentity) and packages/main/src/core/pre-review-live-proof.ts:58-119 (isCanonicalPreReviewCaseId record-ID scoping): neither predicate is referenced by name in any file under packages/main/tests/, and no CHK-001..CHK-005 verificationIntent names either behavior directly. sameAuditedAttestationIdentity first appears only in merge commit a2e4e92631 (present in neither parent, i.e. hand-authored during conflict resolution) and governs a real behavior split -- a note-only checklist_update on a mechanical:true receipt drops the receipt (sameEvidenceSemantics is note-sensitive) while the same note-only update on a mechanical:false attestation keeps it (sameAuditedAttestationIdentity ignores note) -- with no direct unit exercising either branch of that split. isCanonicalPreReviewCaseId is exercised only transitively through pre_review_check_read inside the F-247 / F-249-series tests in causal-evidence.test.mjs, and those two tests are themselves currently failing at live HEAD (see B-5a15:F-329), so the only coverage path that reaches this new scoping logic cannot currently demonstrate it behaves as intended. Both are unclaimed by any checklist item's Files/scope declaration and neither is must-priority, so this is recorded as a deferred, non-blocking coverage gap rather than expanded into this story's scope: a follow-up should add a direct logic_test for sameAuditedAttestationIdentity's note-tolerant carry-forward vs sameEvidenceSemantics's note-sensitive drop, and a direct fixture-level test for isCanonicalPreReviewCaseId that does not depend on the full pre-review acceptance chain being green.

It governs a real behavior split - a note-only checklist_update on a mechanical:true receipt drops the receipt because sameEvidenceSemantics is note-sensitive, while the same update on a mechanical:false attestation keeps it. Both branches ARE exercised today, but only transitively: tool-executed-evidence-receipt-smoke.ts covers the receipt branch (F-067 case 12d, asserts note drift drops the receipt) and proofstory-acceptance-topology-smoke.ts covers the attestation branch (asserts a note-only update carries the audited reason forward). findings.desc: completeness-gap (topology critic, epoch B-5a15:RI-051 wave 1/3): the three reporting lanes (concept RR-780, quality RR-778, test-coverage RR-779) collectively left the Wave 4 verifier-owned acceptance surface UNREVIEWED, and that surface holds the only currently BLOCKING verdict. Independently executed all four canonical read-only surfaces at HEAD 62f8d51: (1) acceptance_topology_check = pass, basis complete, structuralPass=yes, blocking=no, authority=diagnostic_only; (2) pre_review_check_read = FAIL with PR_ARTIFACT_TAMPERED, PR_COVERAGE_BASIS_CHANGED, PR_PRODUCTION_PATH_UNPROVEN, PR_MUTATION_EVIDENCE_MISSING, PR_MUTATION_DID_NOT_BITE, PR_CONTROL_NOT_RESTORED, PR_TRANSCRIPT_MISSING, PR_AUTHORITY_INADMISSIBLE (mode=observe so blocking=false); (3) acceptance_rollout_report_read = FAIL, receipt=stale, quorum=full-3x2, AR_REPORT_STALE; (4) acceptance_rollout_check = FAIL promotionEligible=false, mode=ENFORCE, blocking=TRUE, receipt=stale, AR_REPORT_STALE. Surface (4) is the decisive omission: it is the only surface in enforce mode with blocking=true, and keyword-scanning all six raw findings of this wave for rollout / AR_REPORT / 3x2 / quorum / enforce / acceptance_rollout returns ZERO hits, so no lane in this wave touched it. The rollout receipt is stale rather than missing and quorum reads full-3x2, so this is a freshness re-binding need (the receipt no longer binds current HEAD), not the degraded-3x1 condition the envelope forbids. The six raw findings are each genuine and each concern DEV-side implementation (causal DAG edge shape F-325, rerun-evidence producer F-327, brand-path regex F-326, finding hygiene F-328, evidence integrity F-329, predicate coverage F-330); none establishes or refutes current acceptance admissibility. Consequently this wave cannot support any acceptance PASS claim: the envelope requires a current signed rollout receipt and the current receipt is stale under an enforce-mode blocking gate. Remediation: regenerate and re-verify the rollout report/receipt against current HEAD and reissue pre_review_check, then re-read all four surfaces before REVIEW->TEST.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED. This was the topology critic's own RI-051 completeness finding: acceptance_rollout_check was blocking in enforce mode with AR_REPORT_STALE, and all three reporting lanes had missed the Wave 4 acceptance surface entirely. ROOT CAUSE was freshness re-binding, not a broken campaign: the runner digest already matched (sha256:c66f8e7b...), and the report was simply bound to HEAD 2687d440 while the tree had moved. REMEDIATION: regenerated the report via acceptance_rollout_report from DEV phase (its only writer; DEV-gated, which is why it could not be done from REVIEW). VERIFICATION, independently reproduced by two agents: acceptance_rollout_check now returns PASS promotionEligible=true, mode=enforce, status=pass, blocking=false, receipt=current, quorum=full-3x2, codes=none; acceptance_rollout_report_read returns ok=true with diagnostics=[]. The RI-058 critic further decomposed the quorum rather than trusting the label and confirmed it is genuine full-3x2, not a degraded 3x1: rounds=3, emittedCount=6, runIds r1/r2/r3 across hosts claude-cli and codex-cli at symmetric 36/36, and the rollout binding materialHash equals the frozen epoch cutoff exactly - precisely this finding's remediation demand. NOTE ON THE PINNED SUITE: the F-249-series test still fails, but NOT for rollout reasons; its first assertion at causal-evidence.test.mjs:2653 is the shared topology gate, which aborts before its own rollout assertions at :2692-2707 execute. Those rollout assertions would be satisfied by current live state. That residual belongs to F-329, not here.

findings.desc: concept-inconsistency: evidence-freshness.ts:52-64 evaluateCausalEvidenceFreshness is a decorative adapter whose parameter surface contradicts the CausalEvidence concept it claims to expose. Its doc comment names it the 'Explicit opt-in adapter for specialized causal consumers', and process fact runtime:causal_dependency_preflight_metrics_gate (process-fact-levels.ts:437) names core/evidence-freshness a co-owner of that gate. But the adapter (a) EXPOSES rerunNodeIds, which causal-evidence.ts:1284-1287 explicitly voids as 'an untrusted assertion' with 'deliberately no effect on correctness metrics or gate admission', and (b) OMITS rerunEvidence, the only input that can admit a rerun via verifyCausalDependencyRerunEvidence (causal-evidence.ts:1280-1283). So the only rerun knob it offers is the inert one, and the working one is unreachable through it. It also omits storyId, previousHeadHash and currentHeadHash, so every decision it returns has identityBinding.storyId===undefined and identityBinding.currentHeadHash===undefined. Runtime-verified against packages/main/dist: an adapter-produced decision gives hasCausalDependencyDecisionIdentityBinding=true but causalDependencyDecisionMatchesCurrentIdentity(d,{storyId,materialHash,storyFilesHash,headHash})=false, because that predicate (causal-evidence.ts:1385-1392) rejects a binding whose storyId or currentHeadHash does not match the supplied current identity. Both named consumers ALWAYS supply both: evaluateCertificationWindowAdmit passes storyId+headHash (certification-window.ts:485-492) and causalDecisionMatchesCertificationSnapshot passes storyId+headHash (certification-window.ts:771-778). An adapter-produced decision is therefore rejected by construction at both gate sites. Evidence this is dead-on-arrival rather than merely not-yet-used: repo-wide grep (excluding node_modules and dist) finds ZERO callers of evaluateCausalEvidenceFreshness besides its own definition, while the real production producer handlers/certification-window.ts:166-177 bypasses it and calls evaluateCausalDependencies directly WITH storyId, previousHeadHash and currentHeadHash. Impact is conceptual, not a live gate bypass: nothing consumes the adapter today and its omissions fail closed rather than open. The risk is that a future specialized consumer reaches for the officially named adapter, gets a permanently unusable decision, and cannot reach rerunEvidence at all. Not blocking this story's acceptance. Recommended: either delete the adapter so callers use evaluateCausalDependencies directly, or widen it to Parameters<typeof evaluateCausalDependencies>[0] and drop the inert rerunNodeIds from the public shape.
findings.resolvedReason: DEFERRED with F-327, to which it is the same family. REPRO: evidence-freshness.ts:53 evaluateCausalEvidenceFreshness is a one-line adapter over evaluateCausalDependencies whose parameter surface contradicts the concept it exposes - it surfaces rerunNodeIds, which causal-evidence.ts:1287 explicitly voids as 'an untrusted assertion' with 'deliberately no effect', while omitting rerunEvidence (the only input that can actually admit a rerun) and omitting storyId / previousHeadHash / currentHeadHash. EVIDENCE: confirmed zero callers repo-wide (grep across packages and scripts, excluding dist, returns only the declaration itself). The real production producer at handlers/certification-window.ts:166-177 bypasses this adapter and calls evaluateCausalDependencies directly with all three omitted identity fields. The wave-2 concept reviewer additionally verified at runtime that an adapter-produced decision passes hasCausalDependencyDecisionIdentityBinding but FAILS causalDependencyDecisionMatchesCurrentIdentity, so it would be rejected by construction at both certification-window gate sites (:485-492 and :771-778). BLAST RADIUS: none. Dead on arrival with zero callers, and fails closed if one were added. WHY DEFERRED: medium severity, no live defect, no gate distortion, unclaimed by any checklist item, and it is the same root concern as F-327 - the rerunEvidence production path was never built, so the adapter that would front it is vestigial. Fixing it in isolation would mean either deleting a public export or changing its signature, both of which belong with the F-327 producer decision rather than ahead of it. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: resolve together with F-327 in the same follow-up story - if the producer is built, give this adapter the rerunEvidence and identity parameters; if CHK-003's promise is narrowed instead, delete the adapter as dead code. ESCALATE IF: any caller starts using evaluateCausalEvidenceFreshness, since it would silently produce decisions that both gate sites reject.

findings.desc: packages/main/tests/causal-evidence.test.mjs:2333-2352 - the evidence for must-intent CHK-005:adversarial:2 is vacuous because its assertion block has no positive control. The intent claims a metrics PASS cannot advance a story to DONE while open findings, missing coverage, dirty tree, or strict whole-tree drift remain. The test builds metricGateFacts with inventory:null and causalDecision:strictMetricDecision, then makes four assert.equal(...admit,false) calls. The UNMUTATED fixture already returns admit:false, so every assertion passes regardless of the mutation under test. Verified mechanically against packages/main/dist: BASE metricGateFacts yields admit=false blockerCode=pre_cert_causal_freshness_required. Line 2349 claims to prove the open-findings blocker but refuses with pre_cert_causal_freshness_required (certification-window.ts:493 fires before the findings check at :516, so openBlockingFindingIds is never read). Lines 2350 and 2351 clear causalDecision but then refuse with pre_cert_inventory_not_finalized (inventoryLineageRefusal at :508 fires because inventory:null), so missingRequiredIntents at :523 and dirtyNonRuntimePaths at :539 are structurally unreachable. Only line 2352 (strict drift) exercises the branch it names. Consequence: three of the four DONE-gate refusal paths this must-intent promises are asserted but not covered; a regression removing the open-findings, missing-coverage, or dirty-tree blocker would leave this test green and the selector B-5a15|CHK-005:adversarial:2|PASS would still be emitted, so the intent-to-evidence mapping overstates coverage. Fix: assert the unmutated fixture admits (positive control) by supplying a FINALIZED inventory and omitting causalDecision, then assert each mutation both refuses AND returns its own expected blockerCode (pre_cert_blocking_findings_open, pre_cert_coverage_missing, pre_cert_dirty_tree, pre_cert_causal_freshness_required).
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED in commit f5c6f8a2f6. ROOT CAUSE: the evidence for must-intent CHK-005:adversarial:2 made four assert.equal(...admit,false) calls against a metricGateFacts fixture whose inventory was null, so the base already refused with pre_cert_inventory_not_finalized and every mutation returned that same blocker. Reproduced mechanically before fixing: BASE, openBlockingFindingIds, missingRequiredIntents and dirtyNonRuntimePaths all returned admit=false with the identical blockerCode, so three of the four named branches were structurally unreachable. FIX: added an admittable positive control (inventory shaped per inventoryLineageRefusal at certification-window.ts:447-468, with a receipt cutoff on the current materialHash/storyFilesHash lineage) and asserted the SPECIFIC blockerCode for each mutation instead of only admit=false. VERIFICATION: probed against dist - positive control returns admit=true with no blocker, and the three mutations now return three DISTINCT codes: pre_cert_blocking_findings_open, pre_cert_coverage_missing, pre_cert_dirty_tree. A regression deleting any one check would now fail the suite, where previously it would have stayed green and still emitted the CHK-005:adversarial:2 PASS selector.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence-freshness.ts:505,535 [high] currentStoryFilesHash ordering regression: extracting currentStoryFileHashEntries changed the hash ordering from a locale-independent byte sort to a locale-sensitive localeCompare, making storyFilesHash both DIFFERENT from main and ENVIRONMENT-DEPENDENT. On main the entries were composed first (path NUL objectId) and then ordered by a bare .sort() (UTF-16 code-unit order); that trailing .sort() was authoritative, and the pre-existing localeCompare inside changedStoryFilesBetween (line 477) was inert because its order was overwritten. The refactor deletes that trailing .sort() and returns entries pre-sorted by left.path.localeCompare(right.path) at line 505, which currentStoryFilesHash now consumes verbatim at line 535. Two consequences, both reproduced. (1) ORDER/HASH CHANGE: for paths [src/a_b.ts, src/a-b.ts, src/A.ts, src/ab.ts] the old order is A.ts,a-b.ts,a_b.ts,ab.ts and the new order is a_b.ts,a-b.ts,A.ts,ab.ts, yielding sha 6fb89972a802063e... vs 55e75b39781df206...; localeCompare folds case and treats - and _ as punctuation, so any story touching paths differing only by case or by -/_ now hashes differently than main computed. (2) NON-DETERMINISM: localeCompare is collation-dependent - LC_ALL=sv_SE.UTF-8 sorts [z.ts,a-umlaut.ts,a.ts] as a.ts,z.ts,a-umlaut.ts while LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 sorts a.ts,a-umlaut.ts,z.ts, so two machines or a small-ICU build can compute DIFFERENT storyFilesHash for an identical tree. storyFilesHash is the binding material for review passes, causal receipts, delivery/init/scope checks and the DONE gate, so a locale-dependent value can spuriously invalidate every signed artifact or mask a real story-owned change. Fix: keep byte-stable ordering authoritative - either sort the composed path NUL objectId strings with a bare .sort() as before, or use a codepoint comparator instead of localeCompare - and pin a regression test over a path set containing case-only and -/_ variants.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/causal-evidence.ts:1332,1406 [medium] evaluateCausalDependencies is the only signing site in the module that hardcodes process.cwd() as its authority root, instead of threading an explicit recorded root. Every other authority path binds a root deliberately: the receipt signs and verifies against key.identity.cwd / receipt.identity.cwd (735, 533), and the preflight records authorityRoot INSIDE the signed payload and re-derives it on verify (952, 1024, plus the report.authorityRoot === authorityRoot equality check), so a preflight signature is self-describing and cwd-independent. The dependency decision does neither: it signs with process.cwd() at 1332 and verifyCausalDependencyDecision re-derives the key from process.cwd() at 1406, with no authorityRoot recorded in decisionCore. Two reproduced consequences. (1) AMBIENT-KEY MINTING: calling evaluateCausalDependencies while cwd is outside any repo causes readOrCreateCausalAuthorityPrivateKey to CREATE a brand-new key under that directory - running it with cwd=/private/tmp created /private/tmp/.proof-or-stop/runtime/lattice-causal-evidence-authority-v1.key - and the resulting decision then self-verifies as valid under that foreign key, so gateAdmissible=true is signed by an authority unrelated to the project. (2) CWD-COUPLED FALSE TAMPER: a decision minted in the worktree verifies true there but returns false after process.chdir() elsewhere, and verifyCausalDependencyDecision has no way to distinguish that from real tampering - certification-window.ts:494/501 and 794 map a false return onto the blocker text "CausalEvidence decision is missing or tampered" and detectCertificationWindowMaterialDrift reports "causal dependency decision is missing or tampered". Today both are latent because currentCertificationIdentity builds and consumes the decision in one process whose cwd is the repo, so this is a robustness/maintainability defect rather than a live gate bypass - but it is one process.chdir(), one --root invocation, or one persisted decision away from either a spurious tamper blocker or an off-repo-signed decision, and it is inconsistent with the two sibling paths in the same file. Fix: mirror the preflight pattern - resolve the root from the decision context (storyId/project root) rather than ambient cwd, record it as an authorityRoot field inside the signed decisionCore, re-derive and equality-check it in verifyCausalDependencyDecision, and add a cross-cwd test asserting a decision stays verifiable after chdir and that an off-repo root cannot mint an accepted decision.
findings.resolvedReason: DEFERRED to a follow-up story; not fixed here. REPRO: causal-evidence.ts:1332 and :1406 - evaluateCausalDependencies is the only signing site in the module that resolves its authority root from ambient process.cwd(), whereas the receipt path threads identity.cwd explicitly and the preflight records authorityRoot inside the signed payload and re-checks it on verify. EVIDENCE: the wave-2 quality reviewer reproduced it - running evaluateCausalDependencies with cwd outside the repo minted a fresh key under /private/tmp/.proof-or-stop/runtime/ and the resulting decision self-verified as valid under that foreign key; conversely a repo-minted decision returns false after chdir, which certification-window surfaces as 'missing or tampered'. BLAST RADIUS: latent. Every production path builds and consumes the decision in a single process whose cwd is the repo root, so there is no live bypass today. The exposure is a future caller (a test harness, a subprocess, or a tool run from another directory) silently getting a different authority root. WHY DEFERRED: medium severity, no current regression, no lifecycle gate distorted today, and no B-5a15 checklist item claims authority-root plumbing. Fixing it means threading an explicit root through evaluateCausalDependencies and its callers, which is a signature change to shared causal machinery beyond this story's scope. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: a dedicated story that gives evaluateCausalDependencies an explicit authorityRoot parameter matching the receipt path's identity.cwd convention, and asserts a foreign-cwd decision cannot self-verify. ESCALATE IF: any caller begins invoking it from a non-repo cwd, or the decision is ever built and verified in different processes.

findings.desc: concept-inconsistency: certification-window.ts:99-115 CERTIFICATION_DOMAIN_DEPENDENCIES declares 'review-subject': [] and its doc comment asserts review-subject is "terminal and compiles from nothing". Editing any of those docs can flip that script's assertions. Reproduced against the real dependencyClosure algorithm (causal-evidence.ts:1100-1114): a review-subject-only change yields affectedNodeIds=[certification-review-subject] only, so certification-integration is reported FRESH while an actual input of it changed. That is a false-fresh in the same gate-distortion class F-325 fixed, and it matters because test:process-fact-contract is DONE-required (full-suite-runner.ts:155 repoRead('test:process-fact-contract')). Fix: either add review-subject to integration's dependency list, or narrow the review-subject path rule / stop claiming terminality and record why the docs-to-integration edge is deliberately excluded.

findings.desc: certification-window.ts:121 models 'test' as terminal ('test' appears in no other domain's dependency list), but the test domain is a REAL upstream input of the source domain, so a test-only change leaves certification-source falsely FRESH. This is the SAME under-invalidation false-fresh class as F-336/F-337, in the one direction those two fixes did not probe. MECHANICAL PROOF: CERTIFICATION_DOMAIN_PATH_RULES classifies packages/main/src/tasks/ as 'test' and packages/main/src/{core,handlers}/ as 'source'. 7 source-domain files hold compile-time ESM imports of test-domain modules (10 distinct modules): handlers/gap.ts:17 imports ../tasks/gap-analyze.js; handlers/truth.ts:19-21 imports ../tasks/truth.js, truth-analyze.js, extract.js; handlers/test-auto.ts:16-19 imports browser-executor.js, profiler.js, trace-store.js, trace-diff.js; handlers/test-runner-core.ts:13 profiler.js; handlers/bug.ts:4 bug-report.js; handlers/task.ts:2 coverage.js; handlers/test-story.ts:17-18 trace-store.js, trace-diff.js. These are shipped production code, not test scaffolding: registry.ts:37 (the CLI command registry) imports createGapHandlers from ./handlers/gap.js, and packages/main/dist/tasks/gap-analyze.js + dist/handlers/gap.js both exist, confirming tsc compiles the edge into the shipped build. CONSEQUENCE: editing only packages/main/src/tasks/gap-analyze.ts yields declared stale closure ['test'] (probed against the committed CERTIFICATION_DOMAIN_DEPENDENCIES), so certification-source is reported FRESH while a module it compiles from changed - causalRerunComplete can then admit the gate on source evidence earned against the OLD tasks code. Exactly the F-337 defect with source/test swapped. NOT A ONE-LINE FIX - adding 'test' to source's dependencies creates the cycle source -> test -> integration -> source (probed; the committed graph is otherwise acyclic), so this needs a design decision: either split src/tasks/ into the library modules that source imports (currently source domain material) versus the *-smoke.ts executables, or break the test -> integration edge differently. Filing rather than treating as terminal-by-assertion, because causal-evidence.test.mjs:1252 now asserts productionClosureFor('test') deepEqual ['test'] with the comment 'a test-only change must not invalidate any other production domain' - that expectation FREEZES this gap in place, the same way the pre-F-336/F-337 expectations froze theirs.
findings.resolvedReason: DEFERRED to a dedicated story; the finding is REAL and independently confirmed, but the fix is a directory-level refactor unclaimed by any B-5a15 checklist item. NOTE ON ID: the CLI minted this as F-337, colliding numerically with the already-FIXED F-337 (test -> integration) from commit 3172e57e16. This record is the SECOND F-337: 'test is an upstream input of source'. REPRO/EVIDENCE (verified independently, not taken on the report's word): handlers/gap.ts:17 imports ../tasks/gap-analyze.js; truth.ts:19-21, bug.ts:4, task.ts:2, test-auto.ts:16-19, test-runner-core.ts:13 and test-story.ts:17-18 do the same across ten test-domain modules. CERTIFICATION_DOMAIN_PATH_RULES classifies packages/main/src/tasks/ as test and src/{core,handlers}/ as source, so these are compile-time source->test edges. It is shipped code, not scaffolding: registry.ts:37 imports createGapHandlers and registry.ts:206 registers it into the live CLI. Consequence: editing only src/tasks/gap-analyze.ts yields declared closure ['test'], leaving certification-source FRESH while a module it compiles from changed - the same under-invalidation class as F-336 and the first F-337. WHY NOT FIXED HERE: adding 'test' to source's dependencies creates the cycle source -> test -> source; I probed it mechanically and confirmed the committed graph is otherwise acyclic. The real fix is splitting src/tasks/ into the library modules source legitimately imports versus the *-smoke.ts executables that belong in the test domain - a directory-level refactor of shared machinery, well outside this story's scope. MITIGATION IN PLACE: an unclassified path makes deriveCertificationDomainInputHashes return undefined (certification-window.ts:159-160), dropping the whole decision to strict whole-tree freshness, so the exposure is a narrow window rather than a general bypass. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: dedicated story that (a) separates src/tasks/ library modules from smoke executables or introduces a distinct domain for them, (b) declares the resulting acyclic edge, and (c) updates the causal-evidence.test.mjs production-closure expectation for 'test'. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/certification-window.ts:803 passes the wrong-shaped object to causalDependencyDecisionMatchesCurrentIdentity, inverting the drift diagnostic. WHY: causalDecisionMatchesCertificationSnapshot (:764-771) correctly MAPS the identity into the parameter shape the checker expects (dependencyGraphDigest / currentInputHashesDigest, per causal-evidence.ts:1376-1377). The re-check at :803 that decides WHICH reason to report instead passes the raw CertificationWindowCurrentIdentity, whose fields are named causalDependencyGraphDigest / causalInputHashesDigest. Those two names do not exist on the parameter type, so causal-evidence.ts:1387-1390 reads undefined and SKIPS both digest comparisons. TypeScript cannot catch it: the parameter type is all-optional and the argument is a variable, not an object literal, so excess-property checking does not apply. CONSEQUENCE: whenever the ONLY mismatch is a digest, the strict mapped check returns false while the loose re-check returns true, so the code reports the frozen/previous binding as the culprit when the CURRENT binding is what actually drifted, and the [causal advisory binding mismatch] marker carried by the correct branch is suppressed. REPRO (executed against packages/main/dist, not reasoned): built a real signed decision via evaluateCausalDependencies with matching previous hashes MPREV/SFH/HPREV and current MCUR/SFH/HCUR, then set current.causalDependencyGraphDigest to a wrong value. Mapped-shape check returned false; the line-803 raw-current check returned true; detectCertificationWindowMaterialDrift returned reason='causal dependency previous binding does not match frozen certification hashes' even though every frozen hash matched exactly and the current graph digest was the sole mismatch. BLAST RADIUS: diagnostic only, NOT a gate distortion. Both ternary branches return drifted:true, so the window is invalidated identically either way, and grep over packages+scripts (excluding dist) shows both reason strings are produced only at :808/:809 and consumed by no test, gate or parser. The cost is misdirected debugging: an operator chasing a certification-window invalidation is pointed at the frozen snapshot when the live identity is at fault. FIX: pass the same mapped object literal that :764-771 builds (extract it into a local and reuse it at :803).
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED (pending commit). Both digest comparisons therefore read undefined and were silently skipped, so the re-check that chooses WHICH drift reason to report blamed the frozen binding when only the current binding had drifted, and suppressed the [causal advisory binding mismatch] marker. TypeScript could not catch it: the parameter type is all-optional and the argument is a variable, so excess-property checking never applies. FIX: map into the parameter shape at the call site, exactly as causalDecisionMatchesCertificationSnapshot:766-777 already does, with a comment recording why the raw pass was wrong. VERIFICATION: build + recursive tsc clean; causal-evidence suite unchanged at 19/21. BLAST RADIUS CONFIRMED DIAGNOSTIC-ONLY: both ternary branches return drifted:true, so the window is invalidated identically either way and no gate outcome changes; the two reason strings are produced only at :808/:809 and consumed by no test, gate, or parser. Graded medium by the reviewer for that reason; fixed anyway because it is a one-line mapping with zero behavioral risk and misdirected drift diagnostics cost real debugging time.

findings.desc: quality-correctness: handlers/checklist.ts:602 evidenceHashesForPersistence uses the STRICT note-sensitive predicate (sameEvidenceSemantics) where the audited branch needs the note-insensitive twin, so a note-only edit on an audited (mechanical:false) evidence row silently REBINDS its freshness hashes to the current tree. B-5a15 added sameAuditedAttestationIdentity:569 as the deliberate note-insensitive twin and forked on it in carryForwardOnDiskProvenance:834-835 (prior.mechanical===true ? sameEvidenceSemantics : sameAuditedAttestationIdentity), but evidenceHashesForPersistence:602 -- added in the same change and run on the same row moments later via checklist_update:2162 then :2167 -- was NOT given the same fork. The two predicates are identical except for the single clause `incoming.note.trim() === prior.note` (compare :543 against :585). Mechanically reproduced against the two predicate bodies: for an audited row where ONLY note changed, sameAuditedAttestationIdentity=true (so :2162 carries mechanical:false + the prior nonMechanicalReason forward, row survives as an attestation) while sameEvidenceSemantics=false (so :602 falls through to `return current` and re-stamps headHash/materialHash/storyFilesHash to today tree). Mechanical rows are unaffected: they take the strict predicate on BOTH sides, so this is a pure asymmetry, not a global hole. This is gate-distorting, not cosmetic: core/evidence-freshness.ts:627-630 checkEvidenceFreshnessForGit decides fresh by comparing the persisted evidence materialHash against the current tree, so a re-stamped stale audited attestation now reports fresh=true. It is exactly the rebind evidenceHashesForPersistence own docblock:588-591 promises to prevent (a caller cannot rebind a real receipt to hashes for a later tree without re-running it), reached through the one field the new twin predicate declared non-identity-bearing. Fix: apply the identical mechanical-vs-audited fork at :602.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED (pending commit). This was MY OWN regression, introduced by the F-333-era predicate split. ROOT CAUSE: B-5a15 added sameAuditedAttestationIdentity (note-insensitive) alongside sameEvidenceSemantics (note-sensitive) and forked on prior.mechanical in carryForwardOnDiskProvenance:834-835 -- but the SECOND consumer running on the same row moments later, evidenceHashesForPersistence:602 (reached via normalizeEvidence from checklist.ts:2167), was left on the strict predicate. REPRODUCED before fixing: for a note-only edit to an audited mechanical:false row, sameAuditedAttestationIdentity returns TRUE so the attestation is preserved, while sameEvidenceSemantics returns FALSE so the freshness hashes are re-stamped to the current tree. That is precisely the rebind the docblock at :589-592 promises to prevent, reached through the one field the audited twin declares non-identity-bearing. GATE-DISTORTING: evidence-freshness.ts decides fresh off that persisted materialHash, so a stale attestation would report fresh. FIX: evidenceHashesForPersistence now forks on provenance exactly as carryForwardOnDiskProvenance does -- audited rows use sameAuditedAttestationIdentity, everything else keeps sameEvidenceSemantics -- with a comment recording why the two consumers must agree. Mechanical rows were never affected (strict on both sides); this was a pure asymmetry. VERIFICATION: build + recursive tsc clean. CREDIT: found and mechanically reproduced by the RI-055 quality lane (RR-803), which traced both consumers rather than reasoning from the diff.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: core/pre-review-live-proof.ts:161 the `if (requireRegisteredBinding) return false;` guard is unreachable from every production caller, so the requireRegisteredBinding parameter of preReviewCaseSemanticMatches:149 is now inert and the docblock:121-138 describes a guarantee the flag no longer carries. All three production call sites (pre-review-live-proof.ts:228-232, :253-257, pre-review-check.ts:199-203) pass requireRegisteredBinding = preReviewCaseRequiresSemanticBinding(record[9], record[1], record[0]) while passing the SAME record[9] as expectedSourceRef. preReviewCaseRequiresSemanticBinding:139 computes its result as preReviewCaseSemanticBindingForSourceRef(sourceRef, kind, recordId) !== null -- the identical call with identical arguments that preReviewCaseSemanticMatches makes at :154. The two are therefore perfectly correlated: requireRegisteredBinding===true implies activeBinding!==null, which returns inside the `if (activeBinding)` block at :155-159 before :161 is ever reached. Mechanically proven, not reasoned: driving the exported pair over all 42 real registered refs (REGISTERED_PRE_REVIEW_ACTIVE_TOPOLOGY_BINDINGS 21 + _TRANSCRIPT_ 21) crossed with each records real canonicalCaseId and all three kinds yields 126 cases where preReviewCaseRequiresSemanticBinding()===true, and in ZERO of them did toggling the flag change the result of preReviewCaseSemanticMatches (positive control confirmed non-vacuous: the same harness with synthetic non-canonical ids produced 0 true cases, so real canonical ids were required to exercise the branch at all). The flag is still live from the smoke at tasks/proofstory-pre-review-check-smoke.ts:413, which passes the literal true, so this is dead-on-production surface rather than fully dead code. NOT a soundness hole: where a binding exists it is still enforced exactly by the :155-159 branch, which is what actually closes the F-339 borrowing hole; this is the vestigial parameter and the now-inaccurate docblock. Recommend either dropping the parameter and its :161 branch, or documenting that only the smoke exercises it.
findings.resolvedReason: DEFERRED; verified real but non-fireable. REPRO/EVIDENCE: pre-review-live-proof.ts:160 () is unreachable from all three production call sites. This is a direct consequence of my own F-327-era scoping change: preReviewCaseRequiresSemanticBinding now returns true only when preReviewCaseSemanticBindingForSourceRef finds a binding, and preReviewCaseSemanticMatches takes the activeBinding branch in exactly those same cases, so the flag and the branch are perfectly correlated. The reviewer proved it with a positive control rather than by reasoning: across all 42 registered refs x real canonical IDs x 3 kinds, 126 cases had the flag true and ZERO changed the result; the same harness with synthetic IDs produced 0 true cases, confirming the control was non-vacuous. ESCALATE IF: preReviewCaseRequiresSemanticBinding is ever widened to return true for refs WITHOUT a registered binding, at which point line 160 becomes live and its semantics matter again.

findings.desc: quality-cleanup: handlers/checklist.ts:2657 verification_run splits its roots inconsistently. It computes preflightFacts against gitCwd while passing cwd: runCwd at :2658, so probeCausalPreflightFacts:426-427 compares an expected worktree derived from authoritativeCwd (gitCwd) against an actual worktree from probeGitTopLevel(input.cwd) (runCwd). When --cwd names a different git toplevel these disagree and causal-evidence.ts:897 raises worktree_mismatch, hard-refusing a legitimate run at checklist.ts:1113. Secondary inconsistency: :2694 commits via commitCanonicalCausalEvidence(gitCwd) while the receipt identity at :1095 was built from runCwd, so the commit snapshot hashes and the receipt materialHash are computed against different trees. Contrast verification_evidence_add:2369-2371, where cwd, the preflight authoritative root and the commit root are all gitCwd -- that call site is internally consistent and this one was not updated to match. Blast radius is bounded and fail-CLOSED: the mismatch can only reject a legitimate run, never admit stale or unexecuted evidence and never yield a false gate PASS, and --cwd is documented as resolving relative paths against the story git root (same-toplevel subdirectories, which do not diverge). Recommended follow-up: thread ONE root -- either pass runCwd as authoritativeCwd and as the commit root, or reject up front a --cwd whose git toplevel differs from gitCwd with an explicit diagnostic rather than an opaque worktree_mismatch.
findings.uncertaintyReason: Divergence requires a --cwd naming a DIFFERENT git toplevel (nested repo or submodule); I did not construct such a fixture, and any ordinary subdirectory of the same worktree yields the same git rev-parse --show-toplevel, so the common path is unaffected.

WHY DEFERRED: medium/suspected, cannot distort a gate toward a false PASS, not a regression of this story's acceptance scope, and unclaimed by any checklist item. Per triage rule 3 it is recorded with evidence rather than fixed here or dropped. The suite therefore covers the attestation-preservation half of the audited pair but not the freshness-hash half.

SPECIFIC GAP: the F-067 block at tool-executed-evidence-receipt-smoke.ts:678-745 is the only place asserting that an exact re-persist KEEPS headHash/materialHash/storyFilesHash (:712-714) and that a semantic mutation RE-STAMPS them (:739-742). It seeds all four rows via checklist_update with no mechanical field, so they persist as mechanical:undefined (confirmed by probe: INT-F067-NOTE/VERDICT/FILE/ATTESTATION all report priorMechanical=undefined) and exercise only the sameEvidenceSemantics else-branch. Nothing anywhere asserts that a note-only edit to an audited (mechanical:false) row KEEPS its original freshness hashes.

The mechanical-row half of F-067 IS covered: tool-executed-evidence-receipt-smoke.ts:561 asserts semantic note drift drops the prior receipt. proofstory-acceptance-topology-smoke.ts:505-521 performs exactly the note-only edit to an audited row but asserts only mechanical/nonMechanicalReason/note carry-forward; that file contains zero materialHash/headHash/storyFilesHash assertions.

IMPACT is bounded and NOT acceptance-blocking: the shipped source behavior is correct, story coverage is otherwise unchanged at 53 intents / 51 must / 0 must-gaps / 0 waivers / 0 fail-results / 0 orphan refs, and the pinned suite is stable at 19 pass / 2 fail with the same two known DEV-gated failures. The risk is regression-only: because the branch is unexecuted, a future edit reverting the audited fork restores a gate-distorting rebind (evidence-freshness.ts decides fresh off the persisted materialHash, so a stale attestation would report fresh) with a fully green suite.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/evidence-freshness.ts:188 isStoryMetadataPath lowercases the candidate path but compares it against NON-lowercased prefixes, so on a case-sensitive filesystem a real source file whose path differs from a metadata prefix only by case is wrongly classified as story metadata and SILENTLY DROPPED from the storyFilesHash material (the filter at :506 excludes it). Direction is OVER-exclusion, which is the dangerous one: a genuine code change under such a path would not move storyFilesHash, so evidence earned against the older tree would keep reporting FRESH instead of going stale - a false-fresh in the value that binds review passes, causal receipts, delivery/init/scope checks and the DONE gate. REPRO (run against packages/main/dist): isStoryMetadataPath('Docs/Story/my-component.tsx') returns TRUE, and isStoryMetadataPath('DOCS/STORY/legit-source.ts') returns TRUE, even though on a case-sensitive filesystem neither is the story metadata directory. Control cases behave correctly: 'docs/storybook/config.ts' and 'docs/story-utils/helper.ts' both return FALSE, so the prefix matching itself is sound - only the case folding is wrong. NOTE ON DISCOVERY: I first hypothesised the opposite direction (that capitalised metadata paths would be under-excluded) and probed it; all six such cases returned TRUE, disproving that hypothesis. The over-exclusion direction above is what the probe actually established. BLAST RADIUS: latent. git ls-files finds no path in this repo matching a metadata prefix under different casing, so it is not exploitable today, and macOS default filesystems are case-insensitive so the paths could not coexist there anyway. It becomes live on a case-sensitive filesystem (Linux CI, or macOS with a case-sensitive volume) the moment any story adds a source directory whose name case-folds onto 'docs/story/', '.proof-or-stop/story/', or 'docs/framework-audit/'. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: compare case-sensitively (drop the .toLowerCase() on both sides), or lowercase the prefixes too and document the trade-off explicitly. The config-derived storyDir branch at :193 already lowercases its prefix, so the two halves of this function are internally inconsistent. WHY NOT FIXED HERE: medium severity, not fireable in this repo, no lifecycle gate distorted today, and no B-5a15 checklist item claims path-classification behavior - fixing it would be unbounded scope creep per the defect-triage rules. ESCALATE IF: any story introduces such a path, or the project moves canonical CI to a case-sensitive filesystem.

acceptance-coverage-basis.ts:262 basisStatus is 'partial' when EITHER diagnostics.length>0 OR blindSpots.length>0, but every AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF diagnostic is automatically converted into a blindSpot before that check runs, so the designed exclusion escape hatch cannot clear it. TRACE: :379 pushes reconcileTopologyWithCoverageBasis diagnostics; :380-384 immediately maps those same diagnostics into additionalSealIssues as code='derivation_diagnostic'; :386 seals them; :387 derivationBlindSpots = [...preSealBlindSpots, ...snapshotSeal.issues]. The exclusion check at :553 (!pathMapped(path) && !excluded.has(path)) only suppresses diagnostic GENERATION, and our ten blind spots already carry the prefix 'snapshot-seal:derivation_diagnostic:inventory:AT_UNMAPPED_SCOPE_REF:...', proving they came through the seal path. CONSEQUENCE: approving all ten exclusions via topology_exclusion_approval_set would leave blindSpots.length>0, so basisStatus stays 'partial', acceptance_topology_check stays 'inconclusive' (acceptance-topology.ts:695), the F-247 bootstrap at causal-evidence.test.mjs:2474 (which only accepts status==='fail') still fails, the pinned suite stays 19/21, and no evidence can earn a mechanical receipt (verification.ts:139 requires exitCode===0). The sanctioned remediation path is therefore INERT for this diagnostic class. HOW FOUND: while preparing the ten approval commands for a human scope-plan approver, I traced whether the approval would actually clear basisStatus rather than assuming it; it would not. I deleted the prepared script rather than have someone sign ten approvals for no effect. NOT A B-5a15 IMPLEMENTATION DEFECT: the ten refs are internal-helper static-call edges (causalCanonical, causalDigest, effectiveCausalEnvironment, resolveCausalToolVersion, verifyCausalPreflight, causalDependencyContextDigests, plus second call sites of the already-declared CHK-003/CHK-004 producers) that plannedPathDeclarations has no construct to declare. RECOMMENDED HANDLING: a framework story that either (a) lets an approved exclusion also suppress the corresponding seal issue so the escape hatch actually works, or (b) extends plannedPathDeclarations to express internal-helper static-call edges and consumers that are local consts, anonymous callbacks, or top-level statements - the same expressiveness gap that blocks F-329's residual three paths. Both symptoms share one root cause. ESCALATE: this blocks B-5a15 from TEST/DONE and will block any story whose implementation calls internal helpers across module boundaries.

findings.desc: CORRECTION to B-5a15:F-345 - its stated root cause is DISPROVEN by direct measurement; do not act on F-345's closure explanation. findings.resolvedReason: SUPERSEDED by B-5a15:F-347 and PARTLY RETRACTED. findings.desc: ROOT CAUSE PROVEN by instrumentation - supersedes the speculative causes in B-5a15:F-345 and B-5a15:F-346. Exactly ONE endpoint fails discovery, and it is a declaration defect in this story, not a framework bug. Method: copied dist to a scratch dir, instrumented producerConsumerRelation and the actualEndpointPathRefs endpoint gate with stderr tracing, and ran pre_review_check against the real store (observation only - re-authored afterwards with the real build, identical artifact, clean tree). MEASURED RESULT: for CHK-002 consumer packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts#commitCanonicalCausalEvidence the gate reports kindOk=false, reachOk=false, exportedCount=0. Every other endpoint of all five planned paths reports kindOk=true and reachOk=true, and producerConsumerRelation returns true (importedCall=true, correct resolved callers) for ALL FOUR non-CHK-002 pairs. The [EMIT] trace confirms CHK-001, CHK-003, CHK-004 AND CHK-005 all emit actual: refs; only CHK-002 is dropped. WHY: commitCanonicalCausalEvidence is a non-exported local const declared at checklist.ts:1606 inside createChecklistHandlers (and a CausalRefreshCommitter property at :1441), so endpointMatchesArtifactKind's source_file branch requiring exportedCallableCount===1 correctly rejects it. The declaration asserts a source_file callable that does not exist as an exported symbol. CORRECT DECLARATION: the canonical import actually runs inside the REGISTERED handler verification_evidence_batch_add (checklist.ts:2444), which encloses the commitCanonicalCausalEvidence call at :2570; so the consumer should be expectedArtifactKind=handler with expectedSymbolOrFact=verification_evidence_batch_add, exactly matching the WORKING CHK-001 and CHK-005 declarations (registered=true, kindOk=true). fileDeclarationRef CHK-002:files:modify:1 already resolves to checklist.ts and needs no change. This refusal is correct anti-self-exemption behavior and must NOT be bypassed. NOTE the earlier claims are retracted: F-345's bounded-closure explanation is false (verifier.ts and checklist.ts are both in the closure with zero blindSpots, and readBoundedSourceSetForTest accepts all four files), and F-346 correctly retracted F-345 but wrongly predicted the defect lay in producerConsumerRelation's disjuncts - the relation is fine; the endpoint eligibility check is what fails, on one endpoint only.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED and verified end-to-end. F-347 recorded the instrumentation-proven root cause: CHK-002's planned-path consumer declared expectedArtifactKind=source_file with expectedSymbolOrFact=commitCanonicalCausalEvidence, which is a NON-EXPORTED local const at handlers/checklist.ts:1606 inside createChecklistHandlers (plus a CausalRefreshCommitter property at :1441), so endpointMatchesArtifactKind's source_file branch (requiring exportedCallableCount===1) measured kindOk=false reachOk=false exportedCount=0 while every other endpoint of all five planned paths measured kindOk=true reachOk=true. FIX APPLIED: the consumer was corrected to expectedArtifactKind=handler with expectedSymbolOrFact=verification_evidence_batch_add (the registered handler at checklist.ts:2444 that lexically encloses the commitCanonicalCausalEvidence call at :2570), matching the form of the already-working CHK-001 and CHK-005 consumer declarations. The write was performed by the DISPATCHED proof-or-stop-verification-intent role in PLAN after a direct checklist_update was correctly refused with [planned_path_writer_not_authorized]; that anti-self-exemption refusal was honored, not bypassed. Lane counts were preserved (happy=2 edge=3 adversarial=4) and the producer plus outputFactRef were left untouched. findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: CHK-002 userSees promises the terminal prints the literal tokens `receiptPersistedBeforeCanonicalImport` and `importRetry commandRerun=0 receiptHash=<unchanged>`, but neither token exists anywhere in the repo in any spelling (grep -irE receiptPersistedBefore|persistedBeforeCanonical|beforeCanonicalImport|importRetry over packages/scripts/docs = 0 hits). findings.resolvedReason: DEFERRED with evidence per defect-triage rule 2 (non-major, non-blocking, recorded not dropped). CONFIRMED REAL but COSMETIC: CHK-002's userSees promises the terminal prints receiptPersistedBeforeCanonicalImport and importRetry commandRerun=0 receiptHash=<unchanged>. I verified the token claim myself rather than accepting the finding as written, and the finding is partly imprecise: grep over packages/scripts/docs shows receiptPersistedBeforeCanonicalImport has 0 hits in any spelling (the finding is right), but importRetry has 21 hits (the finding said neither token exists). What renderCausalMetrics (core/causal-evidence.ts:1431) actually emits is CausalEvidence: intentCount=.. uniqueExecutionKeys=.. commandExecutions=.. cacheHitRate=..% commandReruns=.. commitFailureReruns=.. unrelatedSpecializedRerun=.. affectedNodeRerun=..% falseFresh=.. So the drift is real: the two exact strings CHK-002 promises are not the strings emitted. THE UNDERLYING INVARIANT IS GENUINELY IMPLEMENTED AND MECHANICALLY PROVEN, not merely labeled: importCausalEvidenceReceipt (causal-evidence.ts:1448) validates the receipt BEFORE invoking commit() and returns commandReruns: 0; tests/causal-evidence.test.mjs:773-793 forces a transient commit failure and asserts deepEqual(storeEvents, ['receipt-persist','canonical-import','canonical-import']) with attempts=2, commandReruns=0, revalidations=2, executions=1 ('import retry never reruns command') and receiptHash unchanged. A regression breaking receipt-before-import ordering or rerunning the command would fail that assertion. WHY DEFERRED RATHER THAN FIXED: userSees is a checklist DEFINITION field, frozen after PLAN — checklist_update is not in the REVIEW phaseTools allowlist, so correcting the wording requires a REVIEW->DEV->PLAN round trip plus a re-dispatched verification-intent role, then re-earning the affected receipts, for a purely cosmetic string with zero behavioral risk. That cost is not justified and rule 3 forbids expanding scope for cosmetic all-green. Severity is low, which is advisory from round 2 onward, and no gate consumes userSees text. FOLLOW-UP MUST: in a dedicated story, either make the CHK-002 path print the promised tokens or reword CHK-002's userSees to the strings renderCausalMetrics actually emits (commandReruns / commitFailureReruns). CREDIT: filed by the round-2 concept lane (RR-834), which also self-reported hitting the zsh unquoted --include=*.ts glob trap mid-audit (it printed 0 hits for all 14 symbols, a false verified-absent) and re-ran with quoted globs before reporting.

findings.desc: DEFERRED with evidence (unclaimed scope, transient race, not caused by this story): validate command 113/116 (npm --prefix packages/graph run check) failed with UNEXPECTED_PROJECT_WRITE - 'content of an existing tracked/untracked file changed during the scan'. ROOT CAUSE, measured not guessed: validate writes and COMMITS its own metadata mid-run - commit 5d6f77dafe 'record B-5a15 validate metadata' rewrote .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-5a15/test-evidence.json by 2199 lines plus process-events.jsonl and closeout-write-receipts.jsonl. The graph verify-no-project-writes probe runs AS command 113 inside that same validate invocation, and validate schedules commands concurrently (stderr shows command 113 starting at 134.9s and command 114 at 141.7s while 113 was still running, with 113 ending after both). So the probe hashes the repository, validate's own evidence write lands inside that window, and the probe correctly reports that the inspected repo changed - it is detecting the harness it runs inside, not a defect in the graph command. EVIDENCE IT IS TRANSIENT AND NOT A REAL WRITE LEAK: run standalone on a quiet tree, node packages/graph/scripts/verify-no-project-writes.mjs reports 'repository byte-identical across a full scan (14772 paths hashed)' and NO_PROJECT_WRITES_OK; the full npm --prefix packages/graph run check exits 0 with bench PASS. git status is clean with 0 entries afterwards, so nothing was actually left behind. WHY NOT THIS STORY'S DEFECT: packages/graph is absent from B-5a15's signed scope contract (zero graph paths in allowedModify/allowedCreate/allowedTest) and git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- packages/graph returns 0 files, so this story changed nothing there. 115 of 116 validate commands passed. NOTE the misleading surface that cost two diagnostic rounds here: validate exits 0 even when it fails - the first run exited 0 with a 0-byte JSON and had actually been refused with causal_preflight_refused state_changed_before_launch, and this run exited 0 with allPass:false status:fail. Never read validate's exit code as the verdict; parse allPass from --json. FOLLOW-UP MUST: in a dedicated framework story, either exclude story-metadata paths from the graph probe's hash set, or serialize the probe so it cannot overlap validate's own evidence commit.
findings.resolvedReason: DEFERRED with evidence, and CORRECTING F-349's own original framing: I first called this a one-off transient race. It is REPRODUCIBLE - validate command 113/116 (validate.commands[112], npm --prefix packages/graph run check) failed with UNEXPECTED_PROJECT_WRITE on two consecutive full validate runs, while passing standalone every time. So it is a deterministic concurrency-configuration defect, not a fluke. MEASURED ROOT CAUSE: lattice.config.json declares validate.commands[112] with resources [{class:'git-common-dir', access:'shared'}], and I verified that ZERO of the 116 configured commands declare access:'exclusive'. Commands [112] through [115] all hold git-common-dir:shared simultaneously, and validate schedules them concurrently (stderr: command 113 started at 134.9s, command 114 at 141.7s while 113 was still running, 113 ended after both). Meanwhile validate writes and COMMITS its own metadata mid-run (commit 5d6f77dafe rewrote .proof-or-stop/story/actives/B-5a15/test-evidence.json by 2199 lines plus process-events.jsonl and closeout-write-receipts.jsonl). The probe (packages/graph/scripts/verify-no-project-writes.mjs:115) compares a whole-repo CONTENT digest before vs after its scan and deliberately hashes gitignored paths INCLUDING .proof-or-stop/** (a documented anti-regression choice at :43-49, because that is 'precisely where a write would matter'). So any concurrent sibling command or validate's own evidence write inside that window flips the digest, and the probe reports content changed. It is detecting the harness it runs inside. WHY IT IS NOT A REAL WRITE LEAK: standalone, node packages/graph/scripts/verify-no-project-writes.mjs reports 'repository byte-identical across a full scan (14773 paths hashed)' and NO_PROJECT_WRITES_OK; the full npm --prefix packages/graph run check exits 0 with bench PASS (typecheck GRAPH_TSC_CLEAN, anchor-check PASS, ASSETS_IGNORED_OK, CLEAN_TREE_OK); git status is clean with 0 entries after every run. I also instrumented a copy of the probe to name the changed path per-file, and standalone it reported no changed file at all. WHY DEFERRED: packages/graph is absent from B-5a15's signed scope contract (zero graph paths across allowedModify/allowedCreate/allowedTest) and git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- packages/graph returns 0 files, so this story touched nothing there; the fix belongs to lattice.config.json's resource declarations or the probe's path filter, neither claimed by any B-5a15 checklist item. 115 of 116 commands pass and verification coverage is complete (53 total / 51 required / 53 covered / 0 missingRequired). FOLLOW-UP MUST, pick one: (a) declare validate.commands[112] resources access:'exclusive' on git-common-dir so no sibling can write during its scan, or (b) exclude .proof-or-stop/** story-metadata paths from the probe's digest while keeping the rest of the ignored-path coverage, or (c) serialize the probe after validate's own evidence commit. Option (a) is the smallest correct change. ALSO RECORDED: validate exits 0 even when it fails - run 1 exited 0 with a 0-byte JSON after causal_preflight_refused/state_changed_before_launch, runs 2 and 3 exited 0 with allPass:false status:fail. Never treat validate's exit code as the verdict; parse allPass from --json.

findings.desc: CHK-004:happy:2 and CHK-004:happy:3 hold receipts whose pinned selectors no longer emit at HEAD d5be091089, because the HEAD commit re-mutated scope-contract.json AFTER the acceptance basis and pre-review artifact were sealed. findings.desc: MECHANISM NOTE supporting B-5a15:F-351, and a CORRECTION to F-351's prescribed fix ordering. F-351 says 'settle the basis first, then reseal pre-review-check.json against it'. That is not achievable as literally stated, because the basis digest is NOT settleable by regeneration: acceptance_basis_generate auto-commits its own metadata, and the receipt binds headHash, so each regeneration binds the NEW head and yields a DIFFERENT basisDigest. Measured directly on an unchanged tree: basisDigest went sha256:ac4ff9fb -> sha256:4dd05029 across two consecutive acceptance_basis_generate runs with zero source changes, and the receipt's headHash tracked the auto-commit (658777bbd3). The digest chases its own commit, so there is no fixed value to seal against in advance. THE ACTUALLY CORRECT ORDERING, established by reading the consumer rather than guessing: issuePreReviewCheckArtifact (core/pre-review-check.ts:338-341) compares basis.priorPlanBasisDigest against input.planArtifact.basis.basisDigest READ AT RUN TIME. It does not require a pre-settled digest - it captures whatever the PLAN basis is at the moment it executes. So the repair is: in DEV, run acceptance_basis_generate and then pre_review_check BACK-TO-BACK with no intervening basis regeneration, and only afterwards re-earn the two CHK-004:happy:2 and :3 receipts, with no basis-affecting command between the reseal and the earn. Regenerate the basis LAST, not first. WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THIS STORY: the general rule I had been applying ('batch all material writes, then earn') is necessary but insufficient for artifacts whose digest is a function of their own auto-commit. For those, ordering must be consumer-driven: identify which artifact READS the other at run time, and run the reader immediately after the writer. F-350's lesson (acknowledge scope before sealing) and this note are the same family: both are self-referential staleness where the repair action is itself a hash-moving write. pre_review_check is DEV-only (command-policy allowedPhases: DEV), so discovering either condition in REVIEW forces a REVIEW->DEV round trip through a fresh review inventory epoch. NOT INDEPENDENTLY BLOCKING: this note documents mechanism only; the blocking condition is F-351 itself, which remains open and must be repaired in DEV. Filed as a separate note rather than folded into F-351 because F-351 is a reviewer-owned finding and its stated remediation is what needs correcting - editing a reviewer's finding text from the main agent would destroy the audit trail of what the reviewer actually concluded.

(2) The signature is NOT the same: the new resolver takes a 4th explicitBaseHead param, returns StoryChangedFile{path,status,oldPath?,blobId?} rather than StoryFileHashEntry{path,objectId?}, THROWS instead of returning undefined when no merge base resolves, sorts by localeCompare rather than byte order, drops the old Map-based per-path dedupe, and no longer treats git C (copy) status rows as rename-like. I verified the behavior is nonetheless SAFE for all reachable inputs and am filing this as documentation-accuracy only, not a live hash defect: both hash consumers re-sort with a bare .sort() on pre-joined "path\\0blobId" strings (evidence-freshness.ts:379-381 and certification-window.ts:167 byDomain...sort()), which I confirmed empirically restores byte order and diverges from localeCompare; rename rows yield byte-identical hash material under both implementations; C rows are unreachable because every call site passes -M only with no -C and diff.renames is unset; and the caller wraps the throw in try/catch to preserve the return-undefined contract. Fix the comment to name story-aware-validation.ts and to state the divergences plus why each is safe, so a future reader does not assume drop-in equivalence and remove the compensating re-sort or the try/catch.
findings.resolvedReason: FIXED, and the reviewer was right that MY comment was the defect.
