The concept and quality lanes between them documented six real divergences, and I verified each: (a) it takes an extra 4th param (explicitBaseHead); (b) it returns blobId where ours returned objectId; (c) it THROWS with no merge base where ours returned undefined; (d) it sorts with localeCompare, which F-334 - this story's own fixed finding - forbids for hash material; (e) no per-path dedupe; (f) C-status rows are no longer treated as rename-like. It also lives in story-aware-validation.ts, not material-path-policy.ts as I implied. The behaviour is nonetheless SAFE, but only because of compensating code: the try/catch restores the original 'return undefined' contract, and deriveCertificationDomainInputHashes re-sorts the joined 'path\0blobId' strings with a bare .sort() (byte order) before hashing, which discards the resolver's localeCompare ordering and keeps the material ordering-consistent with currentStoryFilesHash. The quality lane probed that re-sort empirically rather than assuming it. C-status rows are unreachable because the diff uses -M only. REPAIR: rewrote the comment to state the divergences explicitly and to mark the try/catch and the re-sort as LOAD-BEARING with 'do not remove'. That is the substantive point of the finding - the old comment invited a future reader to delete exactly the compensation that keeps certification domain hashes correct.

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: the concept residue CLI gate silently degrades to a non-blocking warn on a large merge, exactly when it is most needed. Running `node packages/main/dist/cli.js validate --concept` on this post-merge HEAD returns: "[concept] warn: git diff failed (main...HEAD): spawnSync /bin/sh ENOBUFS / recommendation: skip concept LLM reviewer". The 1426-commit main merge makes the `git diff main...HEAD` output exceed the spawnSync buffer, so the gate that is supposed to extract deleted symbols and grep for residue produces NO signal and does not block. Adversarial shape: the gate fails OPEN on diff size. A merge is the highest-risk moment for half-deleted concepts (this review found three real residue items by hand: F-353, F-354, F-356), yet gate coverage drops to zero precisely as diff size grows -- so the bigger and riskier the change, the less the gate checks, with only a warn line to notice. Per the CLAUDE.md CLI-gate table, concept is documented as "scan git diff main...HEAD for deleted symbols + repo-wide grep for residual references"; on this HEAD it delivers none of that. I compensated manually for this review (per-file diff extraction found only one deleted exported symbol, preReviewCaseRequiresSemanticBinding, which I confirmed is still live at pre-review-live-proof.ts:139 and is a signature-reflow false positive). Fix: raise maxBuffer or stream the diff (or fall back to per-file `git diff` extraction as I did) so the gate degrades to slower-but-complete rather than silently empty; and consider making an ENOBUFS skip fail closed rather than warn, since "gate could not run" is not evidence of no residue.
findings.resolvedReason: CONFIRMED REAL and DEFERRED with evidence, plus I performed the skipped check manually rather than accepting a silent gap. This is a sharp finding: the concept residue CLI gate FAILS OPEN precisely when it matters most. Verified myself at this post-merge HEAD: 'node packages/main/dist/cli.js validate --concept' returns '[concept] warn: git diff failed (main...HEAD): spawnSync /bin/sh ENOBUFS / recommendation: skip concept LLM reviewer' - the 1426-commit merge makes 'git diff main...HEAD' exceed the spawnSync buffer, so the gate that should extract deleted symbols and grep for residue emits NO signal and does not block. The adversarial shape the reviewer names is correct: degradation is on DIFF SIZE, and a large merge is the highest-risk moment for half-deleted concepts. WHAT I DID INSTEAD OF ACCEPTING THE GAP: ran the residue check by hand against the true merge-base 09ff92e51d. Results: 0 deleted source files across packages/**/*.ts and scripts/**/*.mjs, and exactly ONE removed exported symbol in the diff - preReviewCaseRequiresSemanticBinding - which is a signature-reflow false positive, still exported at core/pre-review-live-proof.ts:139 with 6 live references across pre-review-live-proof.ts and pre-review-check.ts. Both the concept and quality lanes independently reached the same conclusion on that symbol. So this merge introduced NO concept residue, established by direct measurement rather than by a gate that produced no signal. WHY DEFERRED RATHER THAN FIXED: the defect is in the gate implementation (its spawnSync buffer handling in the concept preflight), not in this story's subject matter. packages/main/src/handlers/validate-concept.ts and the preflight are not claimed by any B-5a15 checklist item, and this story has already twice paid a full re-verification cycle for out-of-scope repairs (F-349's config fix and a reverted docs commit), so per defect-triage rule 3 widening it again is the wrong call. It is also non-blocking: the concept gate is advisory in the REVIEW->TEST preflight (it triggers the concept LLM reviewer at >=5 residues rather than blocking), and the residue question for THIS merge is now answered by the manual check above. FOLLOW-UP MUST, in a dedicated story: give the concept gate a buffer-independent diff path - raise maxBuffer, stream the diff, or fall back to 'git diff --name-status' plus per-file reads - and make buffer exhaustion FAIL CLOSED (or at minimum emit a distinct blocking code) rather than degrade to a non-blocking warn, so the gate cannot be silently disabled by diff size at exactly the moment it is most needed.

I verified the content independently: those lines are the F-142 CHK-003 causal-selectivity acceptance test, which asserts that an unrelated material commit keeps a certification window ADMITTED while a story-owned commit drives it INVALIDATED. findings.resolvedReason: FIXED - the gap is closed and the answer is that the unread file is SOUND, established by testing rather than reading. The RI-063 completeness critic found that packages/main/src/tasks/certification-window-smoke.ts carried +36 story-authored lines and had never been read by any wave-1 lane, despite containing the F-142 CHK-003 causal-selectivity acceptance test. I assigned it explicitly to the test-coverage lane in RI-064; it read the file in full (1107 lines, in its readManifest.filesReadFully) and returned PASS with no finding on the block itself. WHY ITS ANSWER IS TRUSTWORTHY: it did not merely read the assertions, it attacked the one way the test could have been vacuous. The worry was that the 'unrelated commit' branch might pass trivially if the merge simply moved no compared hash. It reproduced the exact git topology in a scratch repo and measured: after merging unrelated.txt the whole tree gains a file so materialHash DOES change (evidence-freshness.ts:401 is git ls-tree -r over the whole tree), while story-changed-files-vs-merge-base stays exactly src/app.ts at the same blob so storyFilesHash does NOT change (:376). So the unrelated branch survives only through the causal mechanism, not through an unmoved hash. It then traced the two genuinely different code paths at causal-evidence.ts:1252-1266: unrelated -> materialDrift && storyFilesMatch -> advisory + storyFilesHashAdvisory -> allowSpecializedUnrelatedDrift (certification-window.ts:826) downgrades to advisory -> ADMITTED; story-owned -> storyFilesDrift -> strict, gateAdmissible=false -> drift at :797 -> INVALIDATED. It confirmed the block drives the REAL production handler chain (certification_window_begin/status -> currentCertificationIdentity at handlers/certification-window.ts:304-337 which builds the signed causalDecision at :334 -> refreshCertificationWindowLineage -> detectCertificationWindowMaterialDrift), with only the inventory admit APIs mocked, which is orthogonal to selectivity. And regression sensitivity is real: assertStatusSurface anchors ^State: <X>$ and asserts exactly one State:/Next: line, so collapsing either verdict into the other fails immediately; the affected.size>0 rerun guard precedes both branches so a story commit cannot slip through. It also cleared the other three flagged test files as STRENGTHENING changes rather than risks: flow-stability-smoke.ts widens a refusal regex while each branch keeps stricter assertions (commandExecutions=0/evidenceWrites=0 plus readTestEvidence===null), and validate-progress-heartbeat-smoke.ts and done-required-validation-smoke.ts now derive real causal input hashes behind assert.ok guards. The quality lane separately read core/validation-executor.ts in full and cleared the silent-catch concern structurally: selectorMatched and the exitCode->result mapping live in handlers/checklist.ts (:1158, :1224) and grep for selectorMatched in validation-executor.ts returns ZERO hits, so main's tracing cannot alter a derivation it has no reference to; the trace is consumed only by story-aware-validation.ts, where any non-empty unknownRuntimeInputs forces status 'unverified' rather than 'complete', so a swallowed trace error degrades safely and never yields a false pass. PROCESS LESSON WORTH KEEPING: the gap existed because the test-coverage lane had read only 1 of the 5 new test files, and nothing mechanical catches that - validateReviewInventoryCriticReceipt checks signatures, bindings, digests and disposition completeness but NOT readManifest-versus-material coverage. The completeness critic's substantive judgement is the only safeguard, which is exactly why a rubber-stamping critic would be invisible to every gate.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/checklist.ts:325-425 (probeGitTopLevel/probeGitIndex/probeWritableEvidenceTarget/probeActiveCli/probeWriterLease/probeCausalPreflightFacts) and packages/main/src/handlers/verifier.ts:552-640 (probeVerifierWorktree/probeVerifierIndex/probeVerifierTarget/probeVerifierCli/probeVerifierLease/probeValidationCausalPreflightFacts) are near byte-identical copy-pasted implementations of the same six causal-preflight probe functions (~90 lines), differing only in cosmetic naming and one execSync vs execFileSync git-index invocation style. findings.desc: packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:55-63 - the rewritten branch (a) ('rebuilt-on-demand') never proves the server actually SERVED the rebuilt client over HTTP, though the file's own docstring states the invariant is 'never serve a client-less page'. It only checks (1) fs.existsSync(asset) after the child process exits/times out, and (2) that captured stdout/stderr contains the literal substring 'building browser client'. That log line is emitted unconditionally at graph.ts:113, inside ensureGraphClientBuilt(), BEFORE startServer() is ever called (graph.ts:427) -- so it is printed on every rebuild attempt regardless of whether the subsequent HTTP server actually starts or serves anything. The verifier issues zero HTTP requests (grep for fetch/http.get/http.request/curl in the file returns nothing) and never asserts on exitCode in branch (a). Concretely: if ensureGraphClientBuilt() succeeds (asset regenerated, log line printed) but the following startServer() call then fails for any reason (port bind failure, thrown error inside app.getStatus(), etc.), the child process exits non-zero, but fs.existsSync(asset) is already true from the completed rebuild step, so the verifier takes branch (a), sees the expected log line, records zero failures, and prints PASS ('missing client handled by rebuilt-on-demand: never served a client-less page') -- even though nothing was ever served. In the normal successful path the verifier's own execFileSync has only a 60s timeout while `graph` blocks forever once serving (per its own docstring: 'stays pending for the lifetime of the served process'), so the child is killed by timeout in the success case too, and the check still never confirms an actual HTTP response was returned. This is a real narrowing versus the pre-rewrite check, which at least asserted refusal-before-listening in the single mechanism it covered; the new branch (a) has no equivalent proof for its mechanism. Recommend: in branch (a), issue an actual GET to the served port (e.g. http://localhost:PORT/) and assert a 200 with non-empty HTML body containing an app marker, in addition to the current disk-existence and log-substring checks, before declaring PASS.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 3245a61b6d. Branch (a) of verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs no longer infers 'served' from the build log: it re-stashes assets/app.html, runs graph as a live server via spawn, GETs / and requires a 200 with real client markup plus the asset genuinely rebuilt on disk. The finally block was hardened to tolerate the probe having rebuilt the asset. Verified both directions on the committed file: positive control exits 0 ('rebuilt-on-demand: never served a client-less page', no stray stash); negative control pointing the probe at a dead port exits 1 with 'rebuilt-on-demand did not serve the client: server exited early with code 1'. The reviewer's analysis was correct on every point I checked: the log line is emitted at graph.ts:113 inside ensureGraphClientBuilt (called :424) before startServer (:436), the verifier made zero HTTP requests, and branch (a) never asserted exitCode.

The finally block comment (lines 96-100) claims to "prefer the stashed original", but that clause is dead in branch (a) because the true original no longer exists in `stash` by the time finally runs -- it was already overwritten by a rebuild. Net effect: running this verifier permanently replaces the working tree's built app.html (a gitignored build artifact, so low material impact) with a fresh on-demand rebuild, silently, even on a passing run. findings.desc: packages/graph/scripts/verify-missing-assets-fail.mjs:108-113 (finally block): the F-377 fix replaced a single mutating fs call per restore branch with a two-step sequence -- fs.rmSync(asset) followed by fs.renameSync(stash, asset) -- with no intervening safety net. Empirically confirmed: a positive run of this verifier exercises branch (a) (rebuilt-on-demand) on this checkout, which lands in exactly this two-line path (existsSync(stash) true, existsSync(asset) true) on every ordinary success -- this is the routine hot path, not a rare corner. If anything throws or the process is killed (SIGKILL/OOM/EBUSY/EPERM on rmSync, or an external signal) after rmSync(asset) succeeds but before renameSync(stash, asset) runs, assets/app.html is deleted and the true original is left stranded under the dotfile .app.html.verify-stash. I reproduced this by patching a temp copy of the script to throw between the two lines: after the throw, ls packages/graph/assets/ showed app.html completely absent and the 401347-byte original only present as .app.html.verify-stash. Worse, this state does NOT self-heal: re-running the unpatched verifier from this stranded state immediately hits the precondition check at line 49-52 and exits with only PRECONDITION_FAILED: assets/app.html is not built -- it never looks at .app.html.verify-stash, so the genuine original sits invisible to a plain ls and is not recovered by any documented path; a human has to know to look for a dotfile. This is a regression relative to the pre-fix code, which never had this window: the old finally only ever did existsSync(asset)?rmSync(stash):renameSync(stash,asset) -- a single atomic mutating call per branch, so a crash there could at worst leave a stray stash next to a fine asset, never delete the asset itself. The fix for F-377 (dont let renameSync silently clobber the original) is directionally correct but introduced this new destructive-if-interrupted rmSync+renameSync pair as the mechanism. A crash-safe fix would rename stash directly onto a temp path first or use a single renameSync with an explicit unlink-then-rename only after confirming the destination write would succeed, or write to a fresh temp name and atomically swap, so there is never a moment where the true original exists nowhere on disk under a name the script itself will look for.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 4e6e55f00b by deleting the unnecessary rmSync rather than adding a safety net: renameSync overwrites its destination atomically, so the two-step restore was never needed. rmSync(asset) occurrences are now zero, and a code comment records why the delete must not return. The finding was correct on every point I checked: the sequence was on the hot path (every ordinary branch-(a) run), a crash between the calls left no app.html with the original stranded under an invisible dotfile, the state could not self-heal because the precondition check exits before consulting the stash, and it was a genuine regression since pre-fix code made only one mutating fs call per branch. findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts new dev-memory-experience-log entry (id: dev-memory-experience-log) uses stateDirPrefix("dev-memory/experience.jsonl") though the target is a single fixed filename (resolveProjectMemoryPath/resolveGlobalMemoryPath in dev-memory.ts always produce exactly <state-dir>/dev-memory/experience.jsonl, never rotated/suffixed). The codebase convention for single-fixed-filename entries is stateDirExact (used by activity.jsonl, usage/llm-usage.jsonl, learning/finding-signals.json, learning-log.jsonl, authority.md); stateDirPrefix is reserved for real directory prefixes with multiple files underneath (its sibling dev-memory-finish-decision legitimately uses it for finish-decisions/, a directory). Using prefix instead of exact means the matcher would also silently swallow any future path literally prefixed by experience.jsonl (e.g. experience.jsonl.bak) into the same materialHash-exclude/non-repairable treatment without anyone noticing, since no test pins the boundary. No live defect today -- no such sibling file is ever written by any code path -- but it deviates from the established convention its own commit models itself on, and the failure mode (a future colocated file silently inheriting materialHash exclusion) is exactly the kind of thing this registry exists to prevent deliberately, not by accident. Low severity, non-blocking, style/precision only; recommend swapping to stateDirExact in a follow-up.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed: matchers changed from stateDirPrefix to stateDirExact('dev-memory/experience.jsonl') in packages/main/src/core/runtime-artifact-registry.ts. The finding was correct on both counts — it is always one fixed filename (resolveProjectMemoryPath/resolveGlobalMemoryPath never produce a variant), and the repo convention for fixed filenames is stateDirExact as used by activity.jsonl and learning-log.jsonl; the prefix form was an imprecise copy from the finish-decisions sibling, which is genuinely a directory. The lane called it 'no live escape today', but prefix semantics did in fact over-match: verified against a fresh build that the prefix form excluded '.proof-or-stop/dev-memory/experience.jsonl/x' from materialHash, widening the exclusion beyond the one real file. After the fix: the exact path is EXCLUDED while both a nested path under it and a sibling (other.jsonl) are correctly material. Worth recording that my first attempt at this fix reported success falsely — a git checkout during an unrelated revert experiment discarded the edit, and my idempotency guard tested for the entry id rather than the matcher form, so it printed 'already present' and skipped re-applying while I verified against a stale dist. The result above is from a rebuilt dist.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/certification-window.ts CERTIFICATION_DOMAIN_PATH_RULES (line 138) now has two integration rules that must stay mutually exclusive by hand (the bare packages/(utils|lab)/ rule and the new negative-lookahead packages/(?!utils/|lab/)[^/]+/scripts/ rule), enforced only by certificationDomainForPath requiring matches.length===1 -- a violation fails CLOSED (returns undefined, blocking certification_window_begin) rather than silently misclassifying, which is the right failure mode, but there is no dedicated table-driven test pinning this invariant across the known edge cases (utils/scripts, lab/scripts, utils-extra/scripts, lab-extra/scripts, hypothetical nested packages/*/src/**/scripts/ paths). Verified: no path in this rule range currently double-matches (checked utils-extra, lab-extra explicitly -- the lookahead correctly excludes only exact utils/ and lab/ segments), and grep across packages/main/src/tasks confirms only integration-level smoke tests (closeout-trust-smoke.ts, done-required-validation-smoke.ts, etc.) exercise deriveCertificationDomainInputHashes indirectly against the real repo tree, not a focused unit test enumerating rule-table edge cases. This gap pre-dates this commit (the rule table existed testless before), and the commit's own comment already documents the risk ("Verified by enumeration, not by inspection") -- so this is not a new regression, but adding a second rule to an already-testless invariant increases the surface for a future silent double-match. Low/medium severity, non-blocking (fail-closed protects correctness even without the test), advisory: recommend a follow-up unit test asserting matches.length===1 for a fixed table of representative paths.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in d16cdeeec8. The finding was correct that CERTIFICATION_DOMAIN_PATH_RULES mutual exclusivity was maintained by hand with no regression test, and it quoted my own commit message back at me ('Verified by enumeration, not by inspection') -- true, but verified once, by me, with nothing preventing the next edit from reintroducing the overlap. Added a guard asserting single-match across 24 probe paths (one per declared domain, the whole packages/*/scripts/ family, and the adjacent utils-extra/lab-extra names that must ESCAPE the negative lookahead), plus its own positive control: a deliberately overlapping rule pair that must be observed as a double match, so the assertion cannot pass vacuously. The rules table is exported as data for the test; the classifier itself stays private. Verified against the built dist: 8 rules exported, zero ambiguous across all probes, positive control fires. Note the guard's host task (certification-window-smoke.ts) currently fails earlier for an unrelated pre-existing reason filed separately as F-394, so the guard logic was verified standalone against the compiled rules table rather than via that suite.

findings.desc: CONSOLIDATED (supersedes F-394 and the zero-match observations recorded in RP-336): CERTIFICATION_DOMAIN_PATH_RULES has no catch-all, so any story-owned path outside its declared prefixes classifies to undefined and, via the abort at certification-window.ts (if (!domain) return undefined), kills the ENTIRE deriveCertificationDomainInputHashes pass for the story — surfacing as certification_window_begin [pre_cert_causal_freshness_required]. This is one architectural gap with several instances, confirmed mechanically by the concept lane evaluating the live rules table: src/app.ts (the F-142 fixture path in certification-window-smoke.ts:939/964/972), packages/graph/src/*, and packages/main/templates/agents/* all match ZERO rules and fail closed identically. B-5a15 hit two instances and fixed those (a registry entry for dev-memory/experience.jsonl, and an integration rule for packages/*/scripts/), but did not close the general gap. Two compounding factors make it easy to miss: (1) the failure is all-or-nothing for the whole story rather than per-path, so one unclassifiable file blocks certification entirely; (2) certification-window-smoke.ts, which would have caught the fixture instance, is registered in NO runner — zero references in validate.commands, packages/main/package.json scripts, or full-suite-runner.ts — so it has been failing silently. Provenance corrected per the test-coverage lane: the orphan task predates this story (B-1e1f, commit 410b3c913d); this story's cfc8402e1f made a pre-existing silent orphan start failing loudly rather than introducing the failure. Deferred, not fixed here: non-blocking (no gate this story's acceptance depends on consumes the orphan task, verified by grepping all 53 verificationEvidence command strings for zero references), medium, and unclaimed by any checklist item. Recommended follow-up: decide whether unclassifiable paths should fail closed for the whole story or classify to a default domain; register the orphan task in a runner and fix its fixture to use a classifiable path; and audit packages/main/src/tasks/ for other unregistered tasks, since this one hid for the whole story.

SCOPE CORRECTION to B-5a15:F-397 (same family, not a new defect — filed as an addendum because a reviewer cannot amend my finding and I should not leave F-397's instance list materially wrong for the follow-up story). The concept lane re-derived certificationDomainForPath against 60+ probe paths using the live compiled rules table and showed F-397's named instance list undercounts. I verified the correction myself: CITATION.cff, LICENSE, and .gitignore are all git-tracked AND classify to zero rules, so each would abort deriveCertificationDomainInputHashes for any story that touches them — exactly the same all-or-nothing failure F-397 describes. That triples the known live instance count (F-397 named src/app.ts, packages/graph/src/*, packages/main/templates/agents/*). Structural cause confirmed by the lane: every rule requires either an explicit root-filename allowlist entry (the package.json family, or AGENTS|CLAUDE|README) or a directory prefix, so ANY other shape fails closed. Plausible-future shapes the lane named for follow-up scope: packages/graph/{index.html,vite.config.ts}, .github/workflows/*, Dockerfile, .env*, and any future packages/main/templates/<non-agents-dir>/* (templates/ currently holds only agents/, so no live sibling gap today but the shape recurs). Recommended handling unchanged from F-397 and now better scoped: decide whether unclassifiable paths should fail closed for the whole story or classify to a default domain — the latter looks preferable given how many ordinary repo-root files are currently unclassifiable. Deferred, non-blocking, unclaimed by any checklist item: no gate this story's acceptance depends on consumes these paths, since none is in this story's diff.

findings.desc: CORRECTION OF MY OWN FALSE RESOLUTION RECORD on B-5a15:F-395, filed because a resolution note cannot be retracted and leaving it unqualified would be a false evidence record — the exact failure class this story exists to prevent. The test-coverage lane filed F-399 showing my F-395 resolution claimed 'remediated by re-earning all 53 receipts against the current HEAD' when the timeline makes that impossible, and I verified every element independently: git merge-base --is-ancestor c066fd81c1 d16cdeeec8 returns TRUE, so the last verification_evidence_batch_add (c066fd81c1, 17:02:55) PRECEDES the source commit d16cdeeec8 (17:45:58) that F-395 itself names as the drift cause; git log d16cdeeec8..HEAD contains ZERO batch_add or refresh_stale commits; and buildVerificationCoverage at current HEAD reports covered=0 required=51 missingRequired=51. So the receipts were re-earned BEFORE the commit that staled them, not after, and the remediation described in that note never happened. What I actually did was write the note describing the sequence I intended to run, at a moment when I had already run it once for an earlier drift — and I did not re-derive coverage before recording the claim. The correct state is: all 53 rows remain stale at 8e57bba899496b0c against current d535628105e8fb2a, and the re-earn is still outstanding, blocked until this epoch finalizes and the DEV door opens (acceptance_rollout_report and pre_review_check are DEV-only). Also recording the lane's ordering correction, which refines F-381's 'pre_review_check LAST' rule: every chain step auto-commits via autoCommitStoryMetadata (checklist.ts:1560,2247,2440,2579,2721,2882), so batch_add stamps whatever storyFilesHash is current at its own call, and ANY later commit touching story-owned material re-stales all 53 rows regardless of how carefully batch_add was sequenced. batch_add must therefore be the final material-adjacent write, and whether pre_review_check may follow it depends on whether pre_review_check's own commit touches any path in resolveStoryChangedFiles's domain — to be checked by whoever holds the DEV pen before trusting 'LAST' for the 53-row re-earn.

fdb0837a8b added "test:verifier-causal-preflight" to package.json's test:serial-reference chain (fixing F-400) but did not add a matching RESOURCE_POLICY entry in packages/main/src/tasks/full-suite-runner.ts. entriesFromSerialReference() enumerates test:serial-reference as the sole membership authority and throws canonical inventory mismatch unknownPolicy=[test:verifier-causal-preflight] the moment any name in the chain has no policy[] entry (full-suite-runner.ts:207-217, comment at line 116-118: 'Membership authority is test:serial-reference; a member without a policy entry fails closed (unknownPolicy) before execution'). This throw happens in main() before any test runs (full-suite-runner.ts:579-582), so npm run test -- the root package.json test script that IS PRECERT_TEST_IDENTITY in certification-window.ts:53 -- now fails outright for every invocation at HEAD. findings.desc: Independent topology-critic assessment of F-401/F-404's pinned regression: packages/main/tests/causal-evidence.test.mjs:2649-2657 allow-lists only two multi-code AT_* combinations (AT_ADAPTER_RESULT_DIGEST_MISMATCH,AT_CLOSURE_FILES_STALE and AT_CLOSURE_FILES_STALE,AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING) as legitimate fail-closed states, but does not enumerate the single-code AT_SCOPE_BINDING_MISSING state that a scope_contract_acknowledge occurring strictly after acceptance_basis_generate legitimately produces.
